highlights.title: Anduril now says its BlueChip laptop will meet Buy American standards at launch
highlights.summary: On Tuesday, defense contractor Anduril and chipmaker Qualcomm announced a partnership to build laptops entirely in the United States, starting with a single model in 2027.
body: Palmer Luckey says it was always the goal, and now the company is committing to it.

Even a single Made-in-USA laptop would be a surprise, because no major US computer company builds its laptops here — not Apple, not Dell, not HP, not Microsoft. We’re not aware of any company that does.

But we are aware of companies that have briefly and strategically assembled computers here seemingly to appease President Donald Trump. We’re also aware of companies that have promised US jobs only to deliver empty buildings. And we’re aware of at least one fake “US” company that lied to the government about making product domestically.

That’s why we now ask pointed questions when a company says it’s committed to US manufacturing. We asked TP-Link those sorts of questions just over a week ago. On Monday, we asked Anduril founder Palmer Luckey and Qualcomm president and CEO Cristiano Amon those kinds of questions.

highlights.title: Canada women snap eight-game skid against USA to avenge Olympic hockey heartbreak
highlights.summary: Kraemer, Tremblay score first senior international goals. Fillier nets winner after Americans erase two-goal deficit. Canada avenge Olympic heartbreak in worlds tune-up.
body: Canada ended an eight-game losing streak against the United States with a 5-3 victory on Wednesday night in Windsor, Ontario, as newcomers Caitlin Kraemer and Rosalie Tremblay scored their first senior international goals in a rematch of February’s Olympic gold-medal game.

The win marked Canada’s first victory over their archrivals since 2025 and came eight months after the Americans snatched Olympic gold in Milan, where captain Hilary Knight scored the equalizer with 2:04 remaining in regulation before Megan Keller struck in overtime to deny Canada a fifth Olympic title.

Sarah Fillier scored the winner with 8:15 remaining in the third period after the Americans had erased a two-goal deficit at the WFCU Centre. Laura Stacey added an empty-net goal with six seconds left to seal the victory in the first of two exhibition games ahead of next month’s women’s world championship in Denmark.

highlights.title: Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI is ‘going to get worse’
highlights.summary: Asked about AI and the trend of college students booing tech CEOs at graduation ceremonies, Instagram head Adam Mosseri acknowledged in an interview that a lot of people really don't like AI, and it's not just young people and creatives.
body: The Instagram boss said that worries about AI come down to ‘a fear of being left behind in some way.’

It’s not only getting worse, it’s going to continue to get worse. I think we’re going to see more frustration and anger, some of it founded, some of it unfounded, over the next couple of years, and that’s going to make it hard for a lot of people, not just in the industry.

Mosseri claimed Instagram doesn’t rank AI creators differently, but raised the question of ranking quality, saying, “There’s a lot of great AI content out there, there’s also a lot of AI slop. Do we rank AI content as well as we rank non-AI content? Probably not.” Talking about AI slop again after previously bringing it up in a New Year’s slideshow dump, he said he thinks the term AI “slop” is used “too liberally.”

Instagram began cracking down on AI-generated profiles in August, after launching a label for AI accounts earlier this year, but misleading AI content like celebrity deepfakes remains an issue. Earlier this month, Mosseri said Instagram is “actively working out what to do” about AI fakes, but he noted, “I don’t think it’s practical for us to try and ban AI content from the platform.”

highlights.title: 'Slow Horses' Season 7 Confirmed? Release Date, Plot, and Everything You Need to Know
highlights.summary: Apple’s tight spy thriller Slow Horses usually ties up each season-long mystery in six episodes, but the season 6 finale ended with a shocking cliffhanger. If you haven’t read Mick Herron’s Slough House books and are desperate to know what happens next, including which characters will be returning…
body: Yes! Apple has already renewed Slow Horses for two more seasons. It revealed a teaser for the new season after the season 6 finale aired on Oct. 21. Slow Horses has received critical acclaim, racking up three Emmy Awards for Outstanding Writing and Directing, and Apple has made sure new seasons release at a regular clip. The writers’ room for season 7 opened while season 6 was still in production, and season 8 has already been confirmed.

Season 6 of Slow Horses combined the plots of Herron’s books Joe Country and Slough House, following the failed MI5 agents of Slough House as they’re hunted by elite Russian operatives. The Russians seek revenge for an assassination authorized by MI5’s new director Diana Taverner (Kristin Scott Thomas). That mission was funded using money Diana didn’t realize came from right-wing media mogul Damien Cantor (Harry Lloyd). The Slow Horses weren’t actually involved, but Diana framed one of their former members, Sid Baker (Olivia Cooke), for the hit because she considered Sid expendable and wanted to protect the real assassin.

highlights.title: Cate Blanchett Warns Against “Unthinking Certainty” as She Accepts Japan’s Praemium Imperiale
highlights.summary: After picking up her honor — considered one of the most prestigious prizes in the global arts — the two-time Oscar winner will sweep into the Tokyo International Film Festival on Friday to take part in several talk events.
body: Two-time Oscar-winner Cate Blanchett added to her stack of global honors on Wednesday, accepting Japan ’s prestigious Praemium Imperiale award at a black-tie ceremony in Tokyo.
At a news conference ahead of the presentation, the actress used the occasion to reflect on the value of creative uncertainty — and the destructive hubris of its opposite.

Presented by the Japan Art Association, the Praemium Imperiale recognizes lifetime achievement across five disciplines: painting, sculpture, architecture, music and theater/film. Often described as the Nobel Prize of the arts, the honor places Blanchett among good company — past theater and film recipients have included Federico Fellini, Akira Kurosawa, Jean-Luc Godard, Martin Scorsese, Judi Dench and Catherine Deneuve. Ang Lee was the last Hollywood-associated recipient, taking the prize in 2024.

highlights.title: Creating AI value with enterprise context
highlights.summary: Across a business, any number of AI platforms, systems, and tools may be at work simultaneously—for example, AI-powered customer platforms, conversational assistants, and workflow and process automation tools. Each one is sophisticated, advanced, and quick to respond.
body: An MIT Technology Review Insights poll finds that while every organization surveyed is using AI today to some degree, fewer than one in five (16%) are extracting transformative value from their deployments. The largest percentage of respondents (40%) say they are seeing moderate gains in specific tasks or teams, while 21% report meaningful gains, leaving 23% that are seeing minimal returns or none at all.

Companies are mostly still piloting AI use cases (according to 38% of respondents) or using it to assist employees’ work with tools like co-pilots or chat assistants (35%). Just 12% of enterprises have AI agents in production and 3% say they are using AI to do most of the work in key processes.

“There’s a big gap between what the models are capable of and how the models are actually being useful inside organizations,” says Prukalpa Sankar, co-founder of Atlan. “For every real-life intent and purpose, artificial general intelligence is already here. It’s just not really useful in most companies today.”

highlights.title: 'Stutter' penalty back in the spotlight after Barco miss costs Chelsea
highlights.summary: The stuttering run-up for penalties has been called 'naive' as players continue to try to deceive goalkeepers with a stop-start approach - but why?
body: The pros and cons of a stuttering run-up are under debate after two crucial penalty misses in the Carabao Cup last 16.
Chelsea midfielder Valentin Barco missed the Blues' fourth penalty in their entertaining shootout defeat by Liverpool when he hit the post after a stuttered run-up.
Xabi Alonso's side would be in the EFL Cup quarter-finals had he scored, but they crashed out as defender Wesley Fofana sent one in sudden death high into the Kop at Anfield.
Barco's miss came after Arsenal midfielder Bruno Guimaraes had his spot-kick saved after a similar 'stutter' run-up as the Gunners crashed out against League Two Fleetwood Town on Tuesday night.

highlights.title: All ribbon locations in Phantom Blade Zero
highlights.summary: If you find all the ribbons in the Village of Lu you will complete an important Phantom Blade Zero side quest: "Young Mistress." They were left by Mu Xiaokui, daughter of Soul's master.
body: Here's where to find all the ribbons in Phantom Blade Zero to complete the "Young Mistress" side quest.

When you reach the Village of Lu, you automatically start the "Young Mistress" side quest. To complete it, you must find the five ribbons left in this area by Mu Xiaokui. When you get close to one, you can hear the sound of the bells tied to it. Completing the "Young Mistress" quest adds an extra phase to the Village of Lu's final boss fight. Defeating the modified version of the boss rewards you with the Fiend Saws swords in addition to the Wild Oriole Sword, which you obtain by beating the regular version of the battle.

Although you don't need to find the ribbons in a specific order, you must be sure to complete the quest before the final fight. If you reach the Puppet Testing Grounds area without finding all five ribbons, go look for the missing ones.
Below, you'll find the location of each ribbon and a short explanation of how to reach it. The list has been ordered according to the most likely path you will take as you explore the Village of Lu.

body: Technology giant Microsoft says its profits for the three months to the end of September jumped to more than $36.6bn (£27.5bn), just days after announcing plans to cut its workforce by more than a quarter.
On Monday, the Windows developer said it would offer buyouts to around 60,000 of its workers to cut costs as it pours billions of dollars into artificial intelligence (AI).
Like many other major tech firms, Microsoft is investing heavily in the infrastructure that powers AI even as questions remain over whether such huge spending will pay off.

highlights.title: Microsoft is ending Copilot support on smart TVs
highlights.summary: Nearly two years after LG and Samsung announced at CES 2025 that their latest smart TVs would include access to Microsoft's Copilot, the company is ending support for the AI assistant's functionality on all TVs this year, according to a report by Windows Central.
body: A notification on LG TVs reveals that Copilot functionality is soon going away on all TVs.

The news comes not from an official announcement from LG, Samsung, or Microsoft, but from an on-screen notification that appeared on Windows Central’ s Zac Bowden’s webOS-powered LG TV earlier today. “Microsoft has recently decided to end support for Copilot functionality on all TVs, including the Copilot-enabled feature available on our LG TVs. As a result, the Copilot-enabled feature on your TV is no longer available and may stop functioning shortly,” the notification explains. It doesn’t specify exactly when Copilot will stop working on smart TVs, but says the feature is “scheduled for discontinuation during 2026” and a specific date is “subject to Microsoft’s timeline.”

Last December, LG faced backlash after an update to webOS added an unremovable Microsoft Copilot shortcut to their TVs that opened the AI assistant’s web app in a browser. LG eventually decided to allow the shortcut to be deleted following many users expressing their frustration online with it being added without their approval.

body: The last time Chelsea beat Liverpool, Estevao was the talk of the Premier League.

The Brazilian was still in his first couple of months at Stamford Bridge when his name hit the headlines after he scored the winner against the Premier League champions with practically the final kick of the match last October.
Fast forward 12 months, and Estevao is beginning to attract attention for all the wrong reasons as he struggles to force his way into Xabi Alonso's side.

The 19-year-old, who joined Chelsea from Palmeiras last summer, was conspicuous by his absence on Wednesday night as Chelsea were knocked out of the Carabao Cup following a penalty shootout loss to Liverpool at Anfield.

highlights.title: Where to find the Flesh Lily in Phantom Blade Zero
highlights.summary: Locating the Flesh Lily in Phantom Blade Zero is part of one of the first secondary missions in the game. The "Flesh Lily" is a long quest that you only complete after reaching the fourth area in the game, Pangzhen.
body: To help you complete this quest, we've prepared this guide explaining where to find the Flesh Lily in Phantom Blade Zero.

The Flesh Lily is a key item that you can only obtain after defeating Hua, Deadly Betrothed, an optional boss in the Weeping Creek Valley. You need it to complete the first step of the "Flesh Lily" side quest, which you can start by talking to Yu'er, a character you meet early in the first area of the game.

During the "Against the Flow" main quest, you will find Yu'er. After she asks for help reaching Pangzhen, talk to her and ask about "how to save her father" to start the "Flesh Lily" side mission. The girl will explain that she knows of a medicine that could cure her father, but to prepare it, she needs a rare flower called Flesh Lily. Yu'er has no idea where you can find it and doesn't offer any hints.

highlights.title: ‘The Mosquito Bowl’ Review: Football Heroes Take to the Battlefield in Peter Berg’s Emptily Macho WWII Epic
highlights.summary: No one familiar with the oeuvre of Peter Berg — the action merchant behind the Afghanistan war drama “Lone Survivor” and the improbably pumped-up boardgame adaptation “Battleship” — should approach “The Mosquito Bowl” expecting great restraint or good taste.
body: This pummelling Netflix production seeks pathos amid the gunfire as it tells the true story of four college football stars joining the Marines in the wake of Pearl Harbor, but not one of these noble warriors feels like a real person.

Historical dates are lightly fudged to give the four men a shared soldierly narrative, and so they collectively endure the grueling trials of Parris Island basic training, horrible but familiar from many a military drama, before shipping out to the Pacific, where the shattering, deafening mayhem that awaits them is horrible but familiar from many a war movie. Knowing that he has nothing new to show us, Berg’s solution is to show us ever more of the same, ladling on the frank images of death and devastating injury with relentless rat-a-tat-tat sound design to the point that the film does attain a blunt sensory force.

highlights.title: ‘Like Saddam opened a Cheesecake Factory’: how did the restaurant end up in a Maga fight over ‘elitism’?
highlights.summary: Obama has been accused of ‘snobbery’ over his Trump diss, as people rush to defend the restaurant chain’s ‘affordable opulence’ Around lunchtime on Tuesday, a Rolls-Royce stopped at the intersection of Beverly Drive and Dayton Way in Beverly Hills, California.
body: Up the street, across from the upmarket Erewhon grocery store – home to $21 smoothies – a few diners sat outside an American landmark: the Cheesecake Factory.
The beloved restaurant chain began here in Beverly Hills in 1978; now it has hundreds of locations across the US and Canada. And this week, it’s become the US’s latest surreal culture-war touchstone.

It started when Barack Obama, campaigning for Democrats in Ohio, made a joke that hit Donald Trump right in the real estate. Referring to his successor’s remodeling obsession, the former president said: “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory. Just gold everywhere.”

The joke was about maximalism: Saddam had 100 palaces and loved gold plating, and the Cheesecake Factory, while affordable for many, offers swanky surroundings that a curmudgeon might describe as over the top. While the Beverly Hills restaurant has a fairly staid interior, a nearby location at Los Angeles’s Grove mall has a grand staircase, floral paintings on the ceilings and an ornate balcony.

highlights.title: I Put a Bunch of AI Agents in Charge of a Fantasy Soccer Team. They’re Not Better Than Humans—Yet
highlights.summary: To experiment with AI’s predictive skills, I let Codex loose on a fantasy team. It tried to bench Erling Haaland at first, but it soon learned the error of its ways.
body: I have consulted my AI-powered crystal ball, and it’s telling me that frontier models are going to get a lot better at making predictions in the near future. Just ask my Premier League fantasy team.

A few weeks ago, I deployed a small horde of AI agents to craft and manage an experimental roster. Given the proliferation of AI agents into pretty much every aspect of our lives, I wanted to know if a swarm of bots could put together a winning team.

I first looked at the potential for AI here a few years ago, playing around with a tool from the UK’s Turing Institute that selected teams after modeling previous fantasy league data. Its suggestions were remarkably bonkers—it didn’t incorporate real-world information, like a player’s injury or a team’s change in management.

This time, while on a flight to visit family, I asked Codex for help. First, I fed the model a couple of relevant research papers. Then, I asked it to build a harness—instructions and code that guides different agents through various steps—that would check recent news and run a model to make predictions.

It tried to bench Erling Haaland at first, but it soon learned the error of its ways.

highlights.title: European football: Bayern ease to Cup victory after Kompany leaves hospital
highlights.summary: Kane gets guard of honour before 6-1 win over Magdeburg. Serie A: Inter sink Venezia, Milan lose at home to Bologna. Bayern Munich sailed to a 6-1 win over second-tier Magdeburg in the DFB-Pokal after their head coach, Vincent Kompany, was discharged from hospital earlier on Wednesday.
body: Kompany’s assistant, Aaron Danks, was in the dugout for Bayern for the last-32 tie, while Harry Kane was rested. The Ballon d’Or winner received a guard of honour from his teammates before kick-off in front of 75,000 fans at the Allianz Arena.

Bayern had no difficulty without their star striker, with Michael Olise opening the scoring and adding a second-half penalty. Ismael Saibari, Alphonso Davies, Nathaniel Brown and teenager David Santos Daiber also got on the scoresheet, with Mateusz Zukowski striking for the visitors.

The German Cup holders received good news pre-match, with Kompany able to return home five days after collapsing at training on Friday. The Bayern Munich sporting director, Max Eberl, revealed that the Belgian had been suffering from meningeal irritation.

“We have identified the cause: it is a case of meningeal irritation, which is what triggered the incident last Friday,” Eberl said. “He has now been allowed to go home, where he can continue his rehabilitation … [which] means rest and medication. I am very, very confident that he will be back on the touchline at 100% very soon.”
points: Kane gets guard of honour before 6-1 win over Magdeburg.

highlights.title: Where to find the Outpost cell key in Phantom Blade Zero
highlights.summary: The Outpost cell key is a secondary objective in Phantom Blade Zero that teaches you that exploring the maps thoroughly is worthwhile. As you progress in the story, you will come across plenty of locked doors, and it might take some time before you can obtain the means to open them, as some are…
body: However, you can quickly open the door in this early area by knowing where to look. Below, we explain where you can find the Outpost cell in Phantom Blade Zero.

As you explore the initial areas in the Weeping Creek Valley, you will reach the Outpost Courtyard, an area that became a small enemy camp. After defeating all enemies, you will need to talk to the Baishan Disciples to the right of the locked gate. Before doing so, check to the left of the gate to find a short path leading down to a locked cell.

To find the cell key, progress through the story to unlock the Outpost. Keep following the main path until you find the Outpost bell near Forge, the smith. Climb the stairs near the bell, pass through a small gate, then climb the next flight of stairs. At the end, turn right, and follow the winding path upward to reach a house. Follow the path on its right side.
This new path takes you to another house, where, in front of it, there are two corpses with an orange-glowing orb nearby. Interact with it to collect the cell key.

highlights.title: ULA's Vulcan rocket is set to return to flight on Friday the 13th
highlights.summary: United Launch Alliance announced Wednesday it plans to return its Vulcan rocket to service on November 13, nine months after a solid rocket booster anomaly threw the company's 2026 launch schedule into oblivion.
body: The return-to-flight mission will launch 40 satellites for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation, the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon has booked to deploy the bulk of its network. The mission will lift off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, and ULA said the launch date is pending range approval.

The launch is critical for ULA after its new flagship rocket suffered nozzle failures on its solid rocket boosters on two of its first four missions, most recently during a flight in February. In both cases, the rocket overcame the nozzle failure and completed its mission, but officials at the US Space Force, ULA’s primary customer, lost confidence in Vulcan.

Space Force officials will closely scrutinize Vulcan’s return-to-flight mission. The Pentagon has entrusted ULA’s Vulcan rocket for roughly half of its major launches through the early 2030s. The Space Force certified the Vulcan rocket for national security launches in 2025, then flew two missions on Vulcan before its grounding after the February booster incident.

highlights.title: BioWare Co-Founder Speaks Out on Studio Closure, Mass Effect Cancellation
highlights.summary: BioWare co-founder Greg Zeschuk has spoken out about the closure of BioWare last week, which saw 50 jobs lost as part of 400 cuts across the company, along with the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, which we've now come to learn (via a leaked internal trailer ) was called Mass Effect: Universe.
body: Speaking to 80 Level, Zeschuk lamented the end of the studio but said he went through his own emotional goodbye to the studio after he and fellow co-founder Ray Muzyka departed it on their own terms back in 2012, several months after the launch of Mass Effect 3. “I've kind of gone through all the emotions like long, long ago,” he said. “You have to break from it and kind of go, ‘OK, I've had my emotional moment.’” He continued: “I'm just at a point in my life where I've got my own other business,” he said. “My [beer] brewing business is going really well. I've got a whole other thing I'm doing, and I'm not sentimental or nostalgic. I'm kind of, like, that chapter's closed.”

That said, he certainly had opinions regarding the closure of the great RPG studio he helped build. “I’m not saying it doesn’t hurt and doesn’t suck," he said. "And I think it’s kind of sad. It’s actually, in some ways, saddest for the city of Edmonton, where we’re from, because we were kind of this beacon of hope and excitement and possibility. We showed you could do something really special in a place that was not known for doing things like that.”

highlights.summary: The European Union plans to create the first subsea Internet cable directly connecting Europe to Greenland. The Pan-Arctic Cable project could also extend to Canada and eventually link with Japan and South Korea, notably bypassing the United States.
body: The Pan-Arctic Cable is described as a European Union flagship project in a European Commission joint communication published on October 20, 2026. The policy document describes a new European strategy for the Arctic that supports “a sovereign, secure and resilient submarine cable connection linking Greenland directly to the EU,” while also suggesting that “like-minded partners like Canada” could provide a stepping stone for future cable expansion toward Asia.

“It is interesting that this project is even being considered, because five years ago it would have seemed like not a particularly commercially attractive proposition,” Elisabeth Braw, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council who leads the Threats to the Global Maritime Order Initiative, told Ars. “But the fact that it's being considered is very much on trend and a sign of our times.”

highlights.title: Original Donkey Kong Poster That Was Nearly Thrown Away Sold at Auction for Record-Breaking $329,400
highlights.summary: A 1981 promotional poster for the original Donkey Kong, featuring the first public appearance of Mario, has become the the most expensive piece of original video game art ever sold at auction. But this artwork nearly got thrown out in the garbage.
body: The poster was drawn by artist Leslie Cabarga as an arcade flyer for Nintendo of America, depicting Donkey Kong angrily hoisting a barrel over his head as a determined Mario — then simply named ‘Jumpman’ — makes his way up a building to save Pauline, who cowers in fear behind her hulking captor.

As told in a press release shared with IGN, this flyer has now sold for an eye-watering $329,400, making it the most expensive video game artwork ever sold at auction. That record was previously held by the original cover artwork for Prince of Persia, which sold at Heritage Auctions in 2023 for $63,000 — meaning the Donkey Kong poster blew it out of the water by a staggering $266,400.

The poster inspired a sale of other historic Nintendo artworks titled Landry Pop Auctions' Jumpman: The Beginning of an Icon. This event included original production artwork from Super Mario Bros. and even some of the first illustrations of the game series’ iconic enemies.

highlights.title: 9 Best Hotels in Rio de Janeiro for a Taste of the Carioca Lifestyle
highlights.summary: From grand hotels on Copacabana to intimate retreats in Santa Teresa, these stays capture Rio’s singular mix of beach life, Brazilian design, and warm hospitality.
body: “I live where you vacation” takes on a whole other meaning when, like me, you're based in Rio de Janeiro. I live smack in the middle of South America ’s two hottest beaches—Copacabana and Ipanema—but it’s not the ocean that keeps me in Brazil's buzziest city. It’s the life that happens around it. It’s the sound of the first coconuts being cut open on the beach in the early morning, the sight of barefoot surfers passing beneath my window, and the honey-like melody of bossa nova flowing from a nearby beach kiosk. Not everyone can live here, of course. But luckily, the best hotels in Rio de Janeiro give you a good taste of what it feels like to be a local in Brazil’s most exciting metropolis.
